```json
{
  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "The 90-day paying-customer constraint decides this. Idea B's own sourced evidence (dashp via starterstory) puts the sales cycle at about 5 months of in-person trust-building per closed deal. That timeline misses the window outright. Idea A's channel (long-tail Google Ads) has sourced benchmarks: $3-8 CPC and 3-5% click-to-demo. That makes it a self-serve motion a solo operator can test within weeks.",
    "Idea A's core build is low-complexity (poll, compare to a schedule, validate shape, alert), which suits an AI-agent-run build. Idea B has to match D2DHQ's attrition, escrow and QuickBooks logic, plus wage-law nuance, before it can credibly sell.",
    "Idea B's other channel is weak. The PestWorld 2026 booths are sourced as already sold out, and the brief itself says the ICP is only 'hundreds' of companies and unsuited to performance marketing.",
    "Idea A still shows that budget exists in the category, with sourced pricing: Files.com bundles an equivalent feature at $199-499/mo and Nodinite charges about $3,600/yr. A narrower, cheaper standalone entry point is at least plausible.",
    "Idea B has the stronger proof that customers pay (dashp at ~$100k ARR, D2DHQ's published tiers). That is its real advantage, but the same sources say revenue arrives too slowly for the 90-day goal."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "Idea B's Demand Evidence shows commission disputes, not demand for software. One quote is an anonymous complaint-site post about a single employer underpaying. The other is a litigated $217k commission case. Neither shows a pest control owner seeking, evaluating, or paying for commission-tracking software.",
  "confidence_note": "Low to moderate confidence. Idea A has serious holes of its own. Its demand quotes are 10+ years old (2012, 2016), and the HN seed quote isn't reproduced. The cost of SEO time-to-rank is unsourced. Its own Case Against says the feature is bundled by Files.com and is buildable in 'an afternoon' with cron and Slack. Neither brief offers direct evidence of a buyer paying for the exact proposed product within 90 days. A wins mainly because B's sourced sales-cycle evidence directly contradicts the timeline, not because A's demand is proven."
}
```
